title: Quota ledger fork during rolling upgrade causing tiered rejection spike
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customer-facing outages observed across Hosted and Dedicated during a staged orchestrator rolling upgrade. Several tenants experienced sustained 429s for 12-45 minutes. Root cause traced to a ledger/epoch divergence where upgrade path caused some hosts to apply a new ledger format while others continued to write to the old epoch counter. When requests hit mixed-host routing, the quota admission path interpreted epoch mismatches as stale credit sets and ejected active credits, causing bursts to be rejected and tenants to be unable to recover until manual reconciliation.
reproduction_steps: Stand up an orchestrator cluster with mixed versions (v2026.02 and v2026.03)
Seed a tenant with quota ledger epoch N and credits in-flight (simulate active long-running conversations)
Trigger a rolling upgrade that migrates ledger format and increments epoch on a subset of hosts
Send concurrent requests routed across both old and new hosts with same tenant token

Observe that some hosts consider the ledger epoch authoritative and perform credit ejection while others accept the old epoch, leading to inconsistent admission decisions and repeated 429s until the tenant ledger is reconciled manually
incident_timeline: 2026-03-01 02:12 UTC - First customer alert (high error rates). 2026-03-01 02:19 UTC - Pager duty triggered; SRE pinned to throttling subsystem. 2026-03-01 02:27 UTC - Mitigation: temporarily pinned affected tenants to single-region routing to reduce cross-version traffic. 2026-03-01 02:40 UTC - Identified ledger epoch mismatch between orchestrator versions. 2026-03-01 03:05 UTC - Hotfix deployed to make ledger epoch verification tolerant and auto-reconcile on read. 2026-03-01 03:28 UTC - Traffic recovered; follow-up reconciliation job completed by 03:50 UTC.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation was to pin tenant routing away from mixed-version pools (traffic steering rule). Deployed an emergency compatibility patch to make the quota admission path tolerant of a single-epoch delta and to avoid immediate credit ejection when encountering a higher epoch from a different host. Ramp controls were applied to limit upgrade concurrency until stable reconciliation was validated.
root_cause: During the rolling upgrade we introduced a ledger format and epoch increment that was not applied atomically across the fleet. The admission code had a strict check that treated any epoch mismatch as authoritative stale-state and performed an unconditional eviction of in-memory credits. With mixed-version routing, this caused some hosts to throw away active credits while others still believed they were valid, producing a feedback loop of repeated rejections and client retries that prevented credits from stabilizing.
resolution: Implemented a three-part fix: 1) Make epoch checks tolerant — if an epoch delta is within a compatibility window, perform a read-merge reconciliation rather than unconditional eviction. 2) Add an idempotent ledger-apply routine to ensure repeated apply attempts converge. 3) Add a migration coordinator step in the rolling upgrade to fence tenants being migrated for a short quiesce window, preventing cross-version routing during the critical epoch bump. Released as orchestrator-2026.03-hotfix-1 and runtime-1.27.
test_plan: Unit tests added for epoch-delta branch logic. Integration tests: run mixed-version cluster scenarios in CI with synthetic tenants exercising long-lived KV cache and concurrent requests. Chaos test that randomly routes tokens across old/new hosts while performing epoch bumps and assert no sustained 429s. Add an e2e canary in staging that simulates heavy burst traffic for 30 minutes during a rolling upgrade.
rollout_strategy: Hotfix rolled to a small canary subset of orchestrator nodes for 30 minutes, monitor admission success rate and token-level metrics, then incrementally roll to 25%/50%/100% over 3 hours. Blocker rollback path preserved (automated revert to previous orchestrator image and immediate withdrawal of migration coordinator).
monitoring_and_alerts: New alert: quota.admission.epoch-delta-rate > 0.5% for 5m - Severity P1
SLO impact alert: hosted.request_success_rate drop > 2% over 10m
notes: Follow-up action: run an audit job to detect any other tenants with epoch deltas > 1 and schedule background reconciliation. Update upgrade playbook to include a short fenced quiesce window when changing ledger epoch or format. Consider making epoch bumps piggyback on a two-phase commit for future schema migrations.
